entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: it appears to ask whether candidate crossings between projects can be inspected and pressure-tested without erasing incompatibility, authority boundaries, failed attempts, or evolutionary history.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit 2188ffef41db27307083ea9c27751facf173ea07 added Laws, Failed Seams, Rediscovered Ideas, Evolution tracking, and a Conservation Report surface.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — no public source located in this recovery pass states that SEAMforge completed, was superseded, or became another named project.
entries.reentry_door: Start with src/types.ts, then inspect the application views and the last architectural-analysis commit.

entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit 5142afb2a0cc7cc5813c8b0fc84e164cdd2cb0af established the SEEDFORGE application scaffold and domain model.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — no public source located in this recovery pass states what seedforge became or why development stopped.
entries.reentry_door: Start with src/types.ts and src/App.tsx; the useful body is substantially richer than the absent README suggests.

entries.body_claim: LampPost contains a Traceable Idea Hive / memory-ecology implementation with immutable event and receipt graphs, redaction and capability boundaries, explicit REINTEGRATION_IMPORTED and WITNESS_REINTEGRATION actions, and verifier non-claims.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED/INTERPRETED: the surviving fossil record describes LampPost as testing how interrupted continuity can re-enter through explicit reintegration receipts while limiting what the verifier is allowed to claim.
entries.last_witnessed_change: The application scaffold commit describes a memory-ecology prototype; the later fossil reconstruction identifies reintegration receipts as LampPost's distinctive contribution.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — no public source located in this recovery pass states that LampPost was completed or formally absorbed elsewhere.
entries.reentry_door: Read src/types.ts beside the dated Git fossil reconstruction; treat re-entry as evidence, not proof of an original occurrence.

entries.body_claim: reCURV contains The Recursive Garden, a co-creative video choreography tool with a Soil Ledger, persistent motifs such as spoon/dust/table/backdoor/022100, layered storyboard synthesis, and separate Autodiscography, BananaDash, and Aippy voices.
entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: it appears to ask whether music-to-video composition can grow through a persistent motif-and-soil ecology rather than treating every generation as a disposable prompt/output pair.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit b276cb6eb03a2b745afbf8f37e494e8a5783c951 implemented the Recursive Garden core scaffold.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — similarly named reCURVrePAIR and reMIX-reCURVrePAIR survive, but this pass found no public source proving that either is the formal successor of reCURV.
entries.reentry_door: Start with src/App.tsx and preserve the original video-choreography / soil-ledger particular before comparing it with later reCURV-named projects.

entries.body_claim: pies and 100pies preserve closely matching Paula-centered encounter ledgers: spoken reflections become reviewable extraction proposals; admitted encounters retain revisions and withdrawal; needs and gifts carry permission/disclosure state; connection proposals remain human-reviewable rather than automatic fulfillment.
entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: the pair appears to ask whether repeated acts of sharing food can become a stewardship memory that notices needs and gifts and proposes accountable human connections without reducing people to a score.
entries.last_witnessed_change: pies added spoken-reflection analysis; 100pies later refactored the ledger toward a bounded stewardship model with proposal-based extraction and structured mutual-aid records.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — the two repositories share a strong implementation family resemblance, but this recovery pass found no public source that establishes fork direction, succession, or a formal terminal disposition.
entries.reentry_door: Read the two src/types.ts files side by side, then follow 100pies' stewardship refactor commit without silently treating similarity as genealogy.

entries.body_claim: BananaDash is more than a banana-ripening joke dashboard: its types define provenance-bearing SeedPackets, trace IDs, bounded hops, TAO epistemic modes, IncomingPollen state, and a witness-node set containing Autodisco v20, TranchNode, BananaDash, and the Autodisco.
entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: it appears to test whether a playful local dashboard can also act as an early pollen/witness receiver across the Autodisco/TranchNode ecology without losing packet provenance.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit 8b350516fb9cdb69b29bccc1133a0f6846100b6d added Supabase integration for the pollen ledger and IncomingPollen support.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — no public source located in this recovery pass states whether the pollen-node experiment completed, migrated, or was intentionally left as a specimen.
entries.reentry_door: Start with src/types.ts and IncomingPollenView rather than the generic AI Studio README.

entries.body_claim: A root-level recovery marker explicitly identifies Autodisco v20 as a likely implementation surface for Static Collective First-Listen Radio and points to the governing canon in the-autodisco.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED: the target is a bounded broadcast in which isolated AI DJs genuinely hear playlist windows for the first time before any cross-DJ exchange, with performer-originated voices and generation provenance.
entries.last_witnessed_change: The root marker records the initial implementation question: where to insert a reversible radio route or mode without disturbing existing Autodisco behavior.
entries.disposition: PARTIALLY DECLARED — the repository's role as a likely implementation surface is explicit and canon authority is explicitly elsewhere; completion of the implementation is not asserted.
entries.reentry_door: Open FIRST-LISTEN-RADIO.md before trusting the generic README.

entries.body_claim: jublEchat now contains a substantial provenance-first idea workspace: ideas/artifacts/events/edges, exact ancestry/currentness checks, Nearby Growth derivation, Residual Lineage, external-artifact export, and boundary tests.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED/INFERRED: its present body is an attributable collaborative idea ecology where currentness, nearby growth, historical residue, and synthesis remain inspectable rather than silently becoming authority.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit 076a26b8e6250a44818c58f0c9ca0c7c67de6bca added Residual Lineage v0 as a deterministic read-only historical projection that fails closed on contradictory residue.
entries.disposition: NO ENDING ASSERTED — executable body and landed history exist. The recovery problem here is a prehistoric README, not evidence that the project is dead.
entries.reentry_door: Ignore the one-line README first; enter through src/App.tsx, the ledger helpers, Nearby Growth, and Residual Lineage.

entries.body_claim: ChronoQuest contains a playable AI-assisted RPG surface with persistent character state, inventory and quests, generated story turns and scene images, real-world habits that can be translated into narrative actions, a community-help tavern surface, and Markdown adventure-journal export.
entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: it appears to ask whether ordinary real-world habits and mutual-aid actions can become consequential RPG actions inside an evolving generated story rather than living in a separate productivity layer.
entries.last_witnessed_change: The surviving main-branch application and type system implement the game loop, real-world habit mapping, community-help requests, and story/journal persistence surface; no README currently explains that body.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — this recovery pass found no public source stating that ChronoQuest completed, moved into another world project, or was intentionally retired.
entries.reentry_door: Start with src/App.tsx and src/types.ts; the real-world-habit → narrative-action seam is the most distinctive surviving mechanism.

entries.body_claim: BnanaGram preserves a full Telegram Web K codebase, but its root README and package metadata remain upstream Telegram material; this pass did not locate a project-owned front door explaining what the Static Collective changed or intended to change in that carrier.
entries.purpose_claim: UNKNOWN / WEAK INFERENCE: the repository name and the separately documented BananaGram-Gram-to-Fork make a Telegram-based participation experiment plausible, but that adjacency is not enough to establish BnanaGram's intended role or a successor relation.
entries.last_witnessed_change: The visible root still presents Telegram Web K development/build instructions rather than a Static Collective contract. A neighboring repository, BananaGram-Gram-to-Fork, explicitly describes a parent-focused Telegram/Jubilee participation fork.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — no public source located in this pass proves whether BnanaGram is an untouched upstream carrier, an abandoned fork attempt, or an ancestor/sibling of BananaGram-Gram-to-Fork.
entries.reentry_door: Treat the upstream Telegram body as carrier evidence only. Compare it with BananaGram-Gram-to-Fork, but do not promote that comparison into lineage without a source.

entries.body_claim: Despite the repository name seedforge-v0, its README declares Jubilee Engine VM v3.2.4-reproducibility: a deterministic non-erasure multi-graph compiler with execution/ontology projections, compiler identity, standalone verification receipts, projection-stability certificates, and explicit verifier non-claims. The app simultaneously exposes a SeedForge Workbench, VM playground, cluster explorer, corpus timeline, and reference-code browser.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED/INFERENCE: the body is a bridge experiment between SeedForge cultivation surfaces and a stricter Jubilee VM reproducibility substrate, testing how creative-memory work can sit above deterministic, independently checkable receipt machinery.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit 43b135c78c4308f628001854edb695906f0c70c3 initialized the Jubilee Engine VM playground with the SeedForge workspace and node exploration surfaces.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — this pass found no public declaration explaining the naming transition from seedforge-v0 to Jubilee Engine VM or its exact relation to seedforge and Jubilee-Engine-VM.
entries.reentry_door: Open README.md and src/App.tsx together; preserve the hybrid identity rather than choosing one name as the whole truth.

entries.body_claim: seedFORK is a coherent Jubilee Unified Studio that composes SeedForge proposal cultivation, reCURV-style repair/refactoring, personalized learning paths, Autodiscography source material, and an append-only SHA-256 witness ledger behind a human Harvest Gate.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED: it tests whether several previously separate creative-memory organs can be composed into one workstation while keeping model output proposal-only and human harvest distinct from generation.
entries.last_witnessed_change: The surviving app wires an Autodiscography-backed Nearby Growth workbench, ledger state, human harvest, album-source attachment, and Jubilee receipt viewing into one interface.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — the project explains what it is but does not publicly state whether this composition was a completed specimen, a precursor to another workstation, or a paused integration experiment.
entries.reentry_door: Start with README.md, then src/App.tsx and the UnifiedWorkbench; this is a composition specimen, not merely a naming variant of seedforge.

entries.body_claim: tranchNode-v1 is an Autodiscography Node: an offline-first, human-authorized song witness space with song/annotation imports, append-only ledger receipts, incoming foreign SeedPackets over a shared witness channel, bounded TAO epistemic modes, explicit human observe/attach/dismiss actions, and an owner auth gate.
entries.purpose_claim: OBSERVED: it preserves songs and creative traces while allowing cross-node inspiration to arrive as attributable, non-canonical foreign seed rather than silently rewriting local material.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit c1ab651e55f85d9f13551c89c1de39097d6b16a4 integrated Supabase and Autodiscography schemas for songs, annotations, and witness events.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — a later active repository named tranchnode now describes a broader model-independent continuity substrate, but this pass found no project-owned source proving that tranchNode-v1 was formally transformed into that repository.
entries.reentry_door: Enter through the song-ledger / foreign-seed / TAO contract in README.md. Compare later tranchnode only as a possible lineage question until a source binds them.

entries.purpose_claim: INFERENCE: the remix appears to push the repair-continuity runtime toward a multi-participant witness-thread environment where generated or imported turns can be attributed, attested, composted, exported, and inspected under explicit authority/provenance state.
entries.last_witnessed_change: Commit b7a15f087f051b63f00194cc32dfd89da9fe0256 initialized the reCURV repair-culture scaffold; the current src/App.tsx now materially differs from reCURVrePAIR even though both repositories expose the same README blob.
entries.disposition: UNKNOWN — the public record does not explain whether this is a fork, remix experiment, successor, or parallel branch of reCURVrePAIR. Exact README identity must not be mistaken for implementation identity.
entries.reentry_door: Compare src/App.tsx between reMIX-reCURVrePAIR and reCURVrePAIR. The delta itself is the useful artifact.
